events.notes: Current first-party page says the first phase is still being constructed, after the historical phase-one 2025 delivery target. No substitute opening date is inferred.
Colt states it is currently building the first phase. This is current construction-state evidence, not a completed construction milestone.

Current official page remains future-tense ('once fully built' / 'will feature') after the historical operating target retained elsewhere in the ledger. Recorded as delayed/unresolved, not as an inferred actual.
Current page specifies a 110MVA HV substation with 80MVA dedicated to LHR1 and National Grid supply. MVA is not converted to MW; design evidence is not energisation evidence.
Current page specifies closed-loop chilled water, air-cooled chillers and economizers. Design evidence only.
Current page specifies diverse fiber paths, MMRs and four points of entry. Design evidence only, not proof of completed network delivery.
atNorth's republication states the first Kouvola data center is expected to start around the turn of 2026–2027. The six-month window preserves the wording without inventing a day.

The current atNorth page still says ready for operation in H1 2026 even though that interval has passed. This is recorded as a stale/current schedule conflict and delayed state, not an actual opening. 430MW is campus power capacity, not asserted live IT load.

Retrospective court evidence: the mayor of Alixan granted Sesterce Group a building permit on 18 Dec 2025. Evidence becomes available to ProofMW on the court publication date. Court states ultimate electrical requirement exceeds 60MW; no exact MW is inferred.

Administrative court suspended execution of the permit pending the annulment case, citing missing environmental impact assessment and serious urban-planning doubts. Suspension is not encoded as terminal cancellation.
Retrospective court evidence: Le Bourget mayor issued the data-center building permit on 13 Mar 2026. Beneficiary name/capacity is not stated in the court communication and is not inferred.

The permit was withdrawn by mayoral order on 12 Jun 2026; on 28 Jul 2026 the administrative court refused to suspend the withdrawal, finding the project non-compliant with height rules. `withdrawn` is a terminal-negative permitting event in the current public record, not a claim that no redesigned project could ever return.
